'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2019–2026 Sudanese transition to democracy]]
**[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
***[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
****[[Rapid Support Forces occupation of the Khartoum International Airport|RSF occupation of the Khartoum International Airport]]
*****Fighting occurs across [[Sudan]] three days after the [[paramilitary]] [[Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF) mobilized. The RSF claims to have captured [[Khartoum International Airport]] and the [[presidential palace]] in [[Khartoum]]. At least 56 civilians are killed and 595 others are injured, with several military personnel and rebel forces also being killed. Several [[Egyptian Army|Egyptian troops]] are also taken prisoner by the RSF. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-65284945 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/15/heavy-gunfire-heard-south-of-sudanese-capital-khartoum (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/16/egyptian-soldiers-captured-in-sudan-to-be-returned-says-rsf (Al Jazeera 2)]
*****[[Chad]] closes [[Chad–Sudan border|its border]] with Sudan as heavy fighting continues between the [[Sudanese Armed Forces|Sudanese military]] and rebel forces. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/chad-closes-borders-with-sudan-amid-armed-clashes/2873302 (Anadolu Agency)]
*****[[Saudi Arabia]], [[Egypt]], the [[United Arab Emirates]], [[Libya]] and [[Qatar]] suspend all planes from inside and outside of Sudan due to the ongoing conflicts and closure of several airports; airlines also fear attacks on their planes mainly in Khartoum. [https://menafn.com/1106019647/Sudan-Unrest-Saudi-Plane-Hit-By-Gunfire-UAE-Airlines-Cancel-Flights (Menafn)] [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2023/04/15/EgyptAir-suspends-flights-to-and-from-Sudan-capital- (Al Arabiya)] [https://libyaobserver.ly/inbrief/berniq-airways-suspends-flights-sudan-over-ongoing-clashes (Libya Observer)]
*[[Papua conflict]]
**Rebels of the [[West Papua National Liberation Army]] kill nine [[Indonesian military]] personnel as the group accuses [[Jakarta]] of refusing to hold [[negotiation]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/rebels-indonesias-papua-say-they-killed-9-army-soldiers-2023-04-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Saikazaki bombing]]
**[[Prime Minister of Japan]] [[Fumio Kishida]] is evacuated during a speech in [[Saikazaki]], [[Wakayama (city)|Wakayama]], [[Kansai region|Kansai]], [[Japan]], after an "[[explosion]]-like sound" is heard. A suspect, believed to have thrown a [[smoke bomb]], is arrested. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/14/asia/kishida-evacuated-japan-explosion-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**At least seven people are killed and another is injured during a [[mass shooting]] in La Palma resort in [[Cortazar, Guanajuato|Cortazar]], [[Guanajuato]], [[Mexico]]. [https://english.news.cn/20230416/0ab1c21ab14a4ce19032ec56d9bc7da0/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Encounter killing]]
**Former [[Parliament of India|Indian Parliament]] member [[Atiq Ahmed]], and his brother Ashraf Ahmed, are [[assassination|assassinated]] on [[live television]] while giving an interview to reporters in [[Allahabad]], while in the custody of police, [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[India]]. In response to the murders, the Uttar Pradesh government bars gatherings of more than four people across the entire state. His son had already been killed in an encounter a month earlier. The government shuts down the Internet access in the [[Allahabad district]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2023/04/16/india/former-indian-lawmaker-killed-intl/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/former-indian-lawmaker-slain-live-tv-while-police-custody-state-restricts-2023-04-16/ (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-65290042 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/16/ex-mp-atiq-ahmed-brother-shot-dead-on-live-tv-in-india (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/lucknow-news/atiq-ahmad-s-son-asad-wanted-in-umesh-pal-case-killed-in-encounter-101681371436932.html (''Hindustan Times'')] [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/gangster-turned-politician-atiq-ahmeds-son-asad-killed-in-encounter-in-jhansi-8554227/ (''The Indian Express'')] [https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/india/up-police-intensifies-security-in-prayagraj-internet-services-shut-sec-144-imposed/articleshow/99530848.cms (''The Economic Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2023 Rutgers University strike]] 
**The [[strike action|strike]] ends as an agreement is reached between faculty and the administration, returning 9,000 staff to work. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/15/us/rutgers-faculty-union-deal/index.html (CNN)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Dubai apartment fire]]
**Sixteen people are killed and nine others are injured by a fire in a residential building in [[Dubai]], [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/4/16/fire-in-dubai-apartment-building-kills-16-people-local-media (Al Jazeera)]
*Twelve people are killed and 28 others are injured when a [[bus plunge|bus falls]] into a gorge in [[Raigad district|Raigad]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]]. [https://www.dailyexcelsior.com/12-killed-28-injured-after-bus-falls-into-gorge-in-maharashtras-raigad/ (''Daily Excelsior'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Germany]] shuts down [[Nuclear power in Germany|its last three nuclear plants]], after the deadline to [[Nuclear power phase-out|phase out nuclear energy]] was delayed by three months due to the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-shuts-down-its-last-nuclear-power-stations/a-65249019 (DW)]
*[[Equatorial Guinea]] confirms six more cases of [[Marburg virus]], bringing the total number of cases in the country to fifteen. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/equatorial-guinea-confirms-six-more-marburg-cases-who-2023-04-15/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Hungary–Ukraine relations]], [[Poland–Ukraine relations]]
**Poland and Hungary ban imports of grain and other food from Ukraine "to protect the local agricultural sector", due to Ukrainian supplies lowering the price of food. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/polish-government-bans-grain-food-imports-ukraine-2023-04-15/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 French pension reform unrest]]
**[[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] signs the pension reform bill into law as protests intensify in the country. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/apr/15/macron-signs-controversial-pension-changes-into-law-after-months-of-protests (''The Guardian'')]
*[[LGBT rights in the Cook Islands]]
**The [[Parliament of the Cook Islands|Parliament]] of the [[Cook Islands]] decriminalizes [[gay sexual practices]] between men. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/488019/cook-islands-parliament-decriminalises-homosexuality (RNZ)]
*[[2023 Dadeville shooting]]
**Four people are killed and 28 others are injured by a [[mass shooting]] at a [[birthday party]] in [[Dadeville, Alabama|Dadeville]], [[Alabama]], [[United States]]. [https://www.al.com/news/montgomery/2023/04/dadeville-birthday-party-shooting-20-people-injured-deaths-reported.html (AL.com)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[SpaceX]] launches [[Earth observation satellite]] TAIFA-1, [[Kenya]]'s first operational satellite, from [[Vandenberg Space Force Base]] in [[California]] on a [[Falcon 9 Block 5]] rocket. The satellite will collect environmental data, including data on floods, droughts and wildfires. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/kenya-launches-first-operational-satellite-into-space-space-x-2023-04-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Twitter]] begins limiting the number of automated messages being able to be sent by the [[National Weather Service]], including emergency alerts, before walking back the changes. [https://www.cnn.com/2023/04/17/weather/weather-news-twitter-automated-weather-tweets-wxn/index.html (CNN)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2023 Grand National]]
**[[Corach Rambler]], ridden by [[Irish people|Irish]] jockey [[Derek Fox (jockey)|Derek Fox]], wins the 175th [[Grand National]] [[Horse racing|horse race]] at [[Aintree Racecourse]]. The start of the race was delayed due to [[Animal rights movement|animal rights activists]] storming the track, with at least 118 people being arrested. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/horse-racing/65245758 (BBC Sport)] [https://www.itv.com/news/granada/2023-04-15/woman-arrested-in-connection-with-protests-at-aintree (ITV News)]
